$comment: The families of processes the reaper (scripts/agent-harness/reaper/) may end, and the processes it spares. Each family names what it is and how a process matches it: one or more match entries, each with an exe pattern read against the process's own executable path, a script pattern read against the script an interpreter (node, python) runs, its first argument that is not a flag, and an args pattern read against the arguments after it; every pattern is case-insensitive, and nothing anywhere in the arguments makes a family by itself. The reaper ends an orphan, a process whose parent pid names no live process or one that started after it (on POSIX also one under pid 1 or the user's subreaper), only when it matches a family, and then with its whole descendant tree. A wrapper family (consoles, POSIX shells, the npx launcher) is read only by what it wraps: an orphaned wrapper goes only with the one reapable process it wraps. It never touches its own ancestry, a tree that holds a spared process, a tree that holds a process younger than graceSeconds, or anything outside the families; it ends within boundSeconds. The families are one-shot runs only: persistent and watch work is never reaped without the owner's word, so turbo run dev or start, the turbo daemon, vitest without run, tsc --watch, tsserver, and the dev servers (next dev, expo start, metro) match no family. Each family is safe to end as an orphan because its only reader is gone: an MCP server talks over the stdio of the session that started it, and its npx launcher only waits on it; vitest, tinypool and jest workers, tsc and esbuild serve the test run or the build that started them; turbo starts again on its next run; git-remote-https serves one fetch, pull or push, over once git is gone. spare names, in the same shape, what reads as an orphan while it still works: a shared MCP proxy, the Git for Windows (MSYS) runtime, whose processes report a parent already gone by design, and tmux or screen, servers detached by design. A family or a spare entry changes only when the owner asks: this is a rule file (the LAW 'A rule is not edited to fit the work', AGENTS.md). See docs/harness.md section 3g.

families.what: An MCP server npx started from its cache: node running a script under _npx/<hash>/node_modules/ of a package whose name ends in -mcp

A known MCP server entrypoint, by the package its script sits in: context7-mcp, next-devtools-mcp, metro-mcp, expo-mcp, react-native-docs-mcp, a @lottiefiles MCP, shadcn mcp, codegraph serve --mcp, and scrapling-mcp
A one-shot vitest run (vitest run, never the watch mode a bare vitest starts) and its tinypool or fork workers
A one-shot turbo run, its native binary or its node shim: never turbo run dev or start, turbo watch, or the turbo daemon
The esbuild service a build, a bundler or a test run started (--service), never esbuild --watch or --serve
A one-shot TypeScript compile, tsc: never tsc --watch or -w, and never tsserver
A one-shot jest run and its workers, never jest --watch or --watchAll
The http or https remote helper a git fetch, pull or push started

A console, a POSIX shell or the npx launcher (cmd.exe, conhost.exe, powershell, pwsh, npx-cli.js, npm exec, sh, bash, env, timeout): read only by what it wraps, never by its own command line, and ended only with the one reapable process it wraps

spare.what: A shared MCP proxy that serves MCP servers to every session over HTTP, however it is launched (the mcp-proxy executable, python -m mcp_proxy, or a node mcp-proxy script): it runs detached by design, so it reads as an orphan while the sessions still use it
A Git for Windows (MSYS) process, any executable of its usr/bin and its shells: the MSYS runtime reports a parent that is already gone, by design, while it still works
tmux or screen: a server detached by design that holds live shells
